questions.q: Recite «فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلصَّآخَّةُ» (80:33) and label the two madds.
questions.a: جَآءَتِ: muttasil (4 or 5); ٱلصَّآخَّةُ: lazim kalimi muthaqqal (6).

questions.q: Harfi means the madd is in ...
questions.a: a letter's name at the start of a surah
options: a letter's name at the start of a surah

questions.q: Madd lazim hunt (pupil PDF): find the lazim in Al-Fatihah, 'Abasa and An-Nazi'at and name the type. Today's rota group recites 79:1 to 8.
questions.a: ٱلضَّآلِّينَ (1:7), ٱلصَّآخَّةُ (80:33), ٱلطَّآمَّةُ (79:34): all kalimi muthaqqal.

questions.q: Extend: which letter names in «الٓمٓ» are stretched to six, and which is not?
questions.a: Laam and meem: six (they have three letters with a madd in the middle); alif is not stretched.
Its name nuun ends in a plain sukoon with no shaddah after it.

questions.q: Which word has madd lazim kalimi muthaqqal?
questions.a: A) ٱلطَّآمَّةُ. Alif followed by a shaddah in the same word: kalimi muthaqqal, 6 counts.

questions.q: Think again: Some surahs begin with separate letters like «الٓمٓ». Why do you think we read them by their names, not their sounds?
questions.a: They are recited as letter names (alif, laam, meem) as the Prophet ﷺ taught; their meaning is known to Allah.
